title: Data Central: the journey of one row
summary: An interactive demo of one synthetic patient record moving through eight stages of the data lifecycle, from generation to a business dashboard, including what happens when a bad batch arrives.

caseStudy.problem: A data platform is hard to explain: the dashboard is visible, but the steps behind it, and what protects the numbers when bad data arrives, are not.
caseStudy.approach: I built a deterministic simulation of a fictional health system's data, all synthetic, and pages on top of it: a scroll-through 3D journey of a single row, a pipeline view, a value page and a brain page covering governance. A quality gate, a dead-letter queue and de-duplicated alerts show how bad rows are held back while production keeps its last good numbers. I worked with Claude from written specs, test-first plans and independent reviews of each task.
caseStudy.result: A public demo anyone can open without installing anything. The pages make no network request at runtime, offline copies are available, and a table maps each component to its Databricks, Snowflake and Microsoft Fabric equivalent.

title: Kyber Praxis
summary: A personal agile board for cards, projects, sprints, check-ins and retrospectives, with backup and restore built in.

caseStudy.problem: A personal agile board: one place to plan my own work in sprints, review each sprint and keep a history.
caseStudy.approach: I built a single-page board with Claude and published it as a private Claude artifact. Cards, projects, sprints, check-ins and retros live in the artifact's own database. The source file is the master copy, and a download button plus snapshots in a backup folder make the data easy to back up and restore.
caseStudy.result: A personal board published as a private Claude artifact. Republishing the one source file updates the live page, and the data can be restored from a backup.

title: Praxis Fasti
summary: A time-block planner with Day, Week, Month and Recap views, plus a Sandbox mode, and a shared demo that opens with sample data.

caseStudy.problem: A planner for time-blocking: plan the day in blocks, then look back at how the time was used.
caseStudy.approach: I built a planner with Day, Week, Month and Recap views, working with Claude from one source file. Two artifacts are built from it: one for daily use, and a demo anyone can open. The demo shows sample data read-only, and Sandbox mode lets a visitor try every feature in their own tab. Build and test scripts keep the two versions in step.
caseStudy.result: A planner in daily use, plus a public demo that needs no sign-in and holds only sample data.

title: Jobscan Board
summary: The tool I built to find and rank job postings for my own job search: it collects postings three times a day, removes duplicates, scores them against written rules and shows the results in a small web app.

caseStudy.problem: Searching for a job means checking many sources, seeing the same postings again and judging each against the same criteria by hand.
caseStudy.approach: I built Jobscan with Claude Code. Scheduled skills collect job postings from several sources three times a day, drop anything that fails my written rules, merge duplicates and skip postings I have already seen. Each remaining posting is scored, put in a tier and explained. A small database-backed board shows the ranked list, and I mark each posting as shortlisted, skipped, applying or applied. The rules live in a plain file, so changing a rule never means changing code.
caseStudy.result: A ranked list I check instead of the sources themselves. A separate demo replays one sample day with made-up data in a neutral setting, so the method can be seen without any real postings.

title: Steppenwolf
summary: A research project that tests whether a systematic model can score altcoins and issue Buy, Neutral, Exit or Short signals, judged on return after trading costs.

caseStudy.problem: The question: can a systematic model score altcoins and issue signals that still hold up after trading costs?
caseStudy.approach: The goal is a system that logs signals and runs a simulated portfolio. It uses free data sources only, stored exactly as received. Each approach is checked by walk-forward testing that keeps delisted coins in, under written protocols with written pass marks, and a final exam period that has not been opened. Every design decision and every failed attempt is recorded.
caseStudy.result: Current state: research only, still in progress. It places no orders and is not ready for live use, and nothing here is trading advice.
